payload.summary: Verified in-canvas dust visualization, DoG-based Detect Dust with precision/recall measurement, accept/dismiss/drag suggestion editing feeding the normal Remove spot + undo path, and selective retouch copy clearing sampled sources for per-frame re-solve. Build, focused tests, full fast suite (1308/1308), and dg validate all pass; no findings, no fixes needed.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Implement A / Visualize Spots as an in-canvas display mode with adjustable threshold, revealing candidate blemishes without changing the rendered image or edit recipe. Integrate with KRMA-661 overlay policy and keyboard routing; retire the DustFinderSheet workflow where it is superseded.
acceptance_criteria.notes: KeyboardShortcuts.swift binds plain 'A' (gated by isRetouchCanvasActive and KeyMonitorPolicy.isPlainCharacterShortcut) to AppViewModel.toggleRetouchVisualization(), which flips retouchInteractionState.visualizationEnabled and recomputes candidates via RenderEngine.retouchAnalysisProxy + RetouchDustDetector. RetouchCanvasOverlay draws visualizationCandidates only under state.shouldShowOverlay (KRMA-661 overlay policy), and the analysis is a display-only overlay: no document/render mutation. DustFinderSheet.swift was deleted and RetouchInspectorView no longer presents it; grep found zero remaining references.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Implement Detect Dust using difference-of-Gaussians blob detection constrained to smooth image regions so texture, foliage, and real detail are not indiscriminately marked. Present dashed suggestion pins distinct from committed spots; clicking a suggestion accepts it and Accept All creates normal editable Remove spots with deterministic seeds.
acceptance_criteria.notes: RetouchDustDetector.detect (Sources/KromoraKit/Models/RetouchAnalysis/RetouchDustDetector.swift) runs a 3-scale DoG over blurred Lab luminance, applies isLocalMaximum + smoothRegion gradient/variance gating to reject textured/edge regions, and derives a stable per-pixel seed. RetouchCanvasOverlay renders dustSuggestions as dashed mint pins distinct from the solid committed-spot markers. RetouchWorkflowCoordinator.beginGesture hit-tests suggestions first; a plain click (no move) calls acceptDustSuggestion, converting to a normal RetouchSpot(mode: .remove) with the suggestion's deterministic seed. acceptAllDustSuggestions wraps all conversions in begin/endUndoGrouping for one undo entry.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Allow suggested positions/size to be adjusted or dismissed before acceptance. Accepted detections must flow through the same source-space region model, undo/history, fill solving, visibility, and rendering path as manually painted spots.
acceptance_criteria.notes: RetouchWorkflowCoordinator's .suggestion gesture case supports drag-to-move and drag-from-edge-to-resize (isResizingSuggestion threshold at 0.65 of radius) prior to acceptance; dismissDustSuggestion/dismissAllDustSuggestions remove suggestions without side effects. Accepted spots become ordinary RetouchSpot values appended to document.retouch.spots, so they use the existing Remove solver, undo stack (verified by testAcceptedDustSuggestionUsesNormalUndoHistory: undoDepth == 1, undo empties spots), visibility, and RenderEngine path -- no parallel code path was introduced.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Measure dust detection precision and recall against KRMA-658's synthetic dust fixtures, document initial operating threshold and false-positive behavior, and retain the manual brush as a straightforward fallback.
acceptance_criteria.notes: RetouchDustDetectorTests.testDetectionRestrictionsAndPrecisionRecallReport runs the detector against RetouchQualityFixtures (KRMA-658) across all backgrounds/soft-dust/speck combinations and prints/asserts precision and fixture-recall; observed and reproduced locally: pixel_precision=1.000 fixture_recall=0.083 fixtures=12. docs/RETOUCH.md's new 'Dust suggestions use a CPU difference-of-Gaussians...' paragraph documents the 0.025 initial threshold, the 0.005-0.12 adjustable range, the measured precision/recall with an honest description of the low recall and its causes, and states the numbers are fixture-scale, not camera-representative. The manual brush remains available and unchanged; the inspector's fallback copy explicitly says so.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Support copying spots to selected frames as part of selective Retouch copy/paste. Preserve region coordinates where frames are related and automatically re-pick/re-solve on each target because fill caches are source-fingerprint scoped. Report completion or unresolved solves without silently applying a stale field from the source frame.
acceptance_criteria.notes: EditClipboardPayload.applying clears spot.source (patch offsets) while preserving region/seed/mode/visibility when the .retouch category is copied, forcing each destination to re-pick/re-solve under its own cache fingerprint (RenderEngine caches are source-fingerprint scoped elsewhere in the codebase). AppViewModel.pasteCompletionMessage appends '; retouch sources resolve per photo' whenever the retouch category is included, so batch paste communicates that fields are not carried over stale. EditClipboardTests.testRetouchRecipesCopyOnlyWhenRetouchCategoryIsSelected and CopyPasteTests exercise this.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Add tests for visualization threshold behavior, detection restrictions and precision/recall report, accept-one/Accept-All recipe creation, undo, dismiss, and cross-frame copy with per-source re-solve. Update docs/RETOUCH.md with the dust workflow and its measured limits.
acceptance_criteria.notes: RetouchDustDetectorTests covers threshold determinism/filtering, precision/recall reporting, and the smooth-region gate. RetouchWorkflowCoordinatorTests.testAcceptOneAcceptAllDismissAndDragSuggestion and testClickingCanvasSuggestionAcceptsIt cover accept-one, Accept-All (grouped undo), drag-move, drag-resize, and dismiss/dismiss-all. CopyPasteTests.testAcceptedDustSuggestionUsesNormalUndoHistory covers undo. EditClipboardTests.testRetouchRecipesCopyOnlyWhenRetouchCategoryIsSelected covers cross-frame copy clearing sampled sources. docs/RETOUCH.md was updated with the A/Detect Dust/Accept-All/dismiss workflow, the DoG detector description, the measured precision/recall limits, and the selective-copy re-solve behavior.

payload.comment: Implemented optional, cancellable Refine to Wire for multi-sample Remove strokes. The proposed ridge boundary remains separate until acceptance; users can keep the original brush geometry, and accepted geometry is stored as a normal RetouchRegion. Single-point dust/speck spots remain ineligible. KRMA-658 generated-fixture measurement: accepted 5/12 oversprayed wire corridors, reducing mean centerline error from 3.93 px to 0.59 px in all accepted cases; ambiguous cases were declined. Synthetic 1–8 px wires and sagging edge-crossing wire tests pass. Checks: swift test --filter 'RetouchWire|PatchMatch|RetouchWorkflow' (20 tests, 0 failures), swift build, dg validate (OK; existing model-name warnings), git diff --check. Commit: 5481f2b.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Add a cancellable wire-refinement step that analyzes a committed rough stroke corridor and snaps the region centerline to the thin dark/light ridge consistent with the surrounding wire evidence, then tightens width to the wire. Preserve endpoints and bends where supported; reject ambiguous corridors rather than warping the stroke unpredictably.
acceptance_criteria.notes: RetouchWireRefiner.refine (Sources/KromoraKit/Models/RetouchAnalysis/RetouchWireRefiner.swift) walks the resampled brush corridor, scores a polarity-agnostic ridge response against both flanks, recenters on connected ridge support, and rejects via .ambiguous/.invalidInput when evidence is weak, a second competing ridge is present, or polarity/contrast medians fail. Cancellation is polled per corridor sample via isCancelled and surfaced as .cancelled. Sagging/bend test (testSaggingLowContrastWireCrossesAHorizontalEdgeAndPreservesBend) confirms bend tracking through a horizontal edge crossing.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Keep the refined region editable and show its proposed boundary before acceptance, with a clear way to keep the original brush region or undo the refinement. Accepted geometry uses the standard RetouchRegion and Remove fill path.
acceptance_criteria.notes: RetouchInteractionState tracks isRefiningWire/wireProposal/wireProposalSpotID separately from the committed document; RetouchCanvasOverlay draws the proposed boundary only while the proposal's spot is selected; RetouchInspectorView offers Keep Brush Region (cancelWireRefinement) vs Accept Refinement (acceptWireRefinement), which only then writes proposal.region into the existing RetouchRegion/RetouchSpot via the normal updateDocument path. Found and fixed one bug in this area during verification (see fixes).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Test straight and sagging 1-8 px wires, deliberate overspray, crossings over roof/branch/horizon edges, low-contrast wires, and ambiguous textured backgrounds using KRMA-658 ground truth. Report when refinement improves wire cases and ensure it does not regress ordinary dust/speck removal.
acceptance_criteria.notes: RetouchWireRefinerTests covers straight/sagging/1-8px widths with deliberate overspray, a low-contrast sagging wire crossing a horizontal roof-like edge, an ambiguous textured-background rejection, cancellation, and single-point dust ineligibility. testKRMA658WireFixturesReportAcceptedAndImprovedCases runs the real KRMA-658 fixtures: 5/12 wire corridors accepted with centerline error 3.93px to 0.59px, 7/12 correctly declined as ambiguous; re-ran and reproduced identical numbers. Wire refinement is opt-in per spot (Refine to Wire button) and does not touch dust/speck spots (ineligible below 2 samples), so ordinary Heal/Clone/dust behavior is unchanged; full RetouchQualityEvaluationTests corpus still passes unrelated to this change.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Record limitations and measured quality in docs/RETOUCH.md; keep this optional and do not make completion of wire refinement a dependency for baseline Remove unless the product workflow deliberately adopts it later.
acceptance_criteria.notes: docs/RETOUCH.md 'Optional wire refinement' section documents the analysis approach, the accepted/rejected KRMA-658 measurements (5/12 accepted, 3.93px to 0.59px), the 1-8px and sagging/edge-crossing synthetic results, and states these are centerline measurements only, not Remove fill-quality claims. The feature is gated behind an explicit per-spot action and RetouchSpot/Remove baseline behavior is unmodified when declined or unused.

findings: [correctness, fixed] RetouchInspectorView.swift: the 'Cancel Wire Refinement' button was gated only on the global interaction.isRefiningWire flag, not on whether the currently selected spot was the one actually being refined. Selecting a different eligible Remove spot while another spot's refinement was in flight showed a 'Cancel Wire Refinement' button that actually cancelled the other spot's analysis, which is confusing but does not corrupt document state (the canvas overlay itself correctly gates on wireProposalSpotID == selectedSpotID). Fixed by also requiring interaction.wireProposalSpotID == spot.id to show the cancel action.

[performance, fixed] RetouchWorkflowCoordinator.refineSelectedSpotToWire only cancelled the wrapping wireRefinementTask, not the Task.detached wireAnalysisTask doing the actual corridor walk; since detached tasks do not inherit cancellation from their spawning task, re-invoking refine while a prior analysis was still running left the old detached analysis running to completion untracked. Not reachable through the shipped UI in its pre-fix form (the cancel-button gating above prevented a second concurrent invocation through normal clicks), but fixed defensively by also cancelling wireAnalysisTask at the start of refineSelectedSpotToWire so re-entry is safe.

payload.title: ThumbnailSwitchLifecycleTests is flaky under the fast parallel test lane

payload.summary: Verified: fix matches the crash mechanism confirmed in both .ips reports, regression tests pass, lane-scheduling gap fixed (InspectorScrollCrashPathTests moved to the serial lane). Filed KRMA-688 for pre-existing, unrelated ThumbnailSwitchLifecycleTests parallel-lane flakiness.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Establish reproducible steps or a deterministic regression harness for the crash path.
acceptance_criteria.notes: InspectorScrollCrashPathTests.swift adds a deterministic harness driving a real NSWindow/NSHostingView through AppKit's display-cycle (window resize + disclosure toggle storms interleaved) that would abort the test process if the app-owned layout invariants regressed. The report's own Last Exception Backtrace has no exception name/reason and no app frames below main, so the exact race (SwiftUI scroll transaction racing AppKit's display-cycle drag-margin flush) cannot itself be reproduced deterministically; the commit and the test docstring say so explicitly rather than overclaiming.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Identify the responsible view/update and the exception or constraint invariant that fails; record whether the trigger is app-owned layout behavior or an OS-specific SwiftUI/AppKit defect.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Verified both .ips crash reports (krma-687-incident-58cc0232.ips, krma-687-sibling-a80dd347.ips) directly: the lastExceptionBacktrace confirms the described path -- NSHostingView.responderNode getter -> AttributeGraph update -> ScrollViewHelper.updateGraphState -> NSHostingView.beginTransaction/setNeedsUpdateConstraints -> _postWindowNeedsUpdateConstraints, invoked from _resetDragMarginsIfNeeded inside NSDisplayCycleFlush. Neither report includes an exception reason, so the fix correctly targets the two concrete app-owned contributors that can schedule an extra scroll-view transaction during that window (a duplicated animation source in InspectorDisclosure.toggle, and a measure/place proposal mismatch in FitsProposedWidth) rather than asserting a specific constraint failure. Whether an OS-level SwiftUI/AppKit re-entrancy defect also underlies this is explicitly left open in the code comments, consistent with the evidence.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Implement a focused fix or documented workaround that prevents the exception during the affected scroll-view, inspector, and window-drag interactions.
acceptance_criteria.notes: InspectorDisclosure.swift: removed the duplicate `.animation(value: isExpanded)` modifier (toggle() already applies withAnimation, so the modifier only stacked a second transaction on the scroll view's content size) and made FitsProposedWidth cache and reuse the exact ProposedViewSize from sizeThatFits in placeSubviews, eliminating a measure/place mismatch that could otherwise keep the scroll content size churning. Both changes are localized and consistent with the crash's mechanism.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Add regression coverage for the identified app-side trigger where it can be exercised deterministically, and verify the affected flow on macOS 27.2 or a matching runtime.
acceptance_criteria.notes: InspectorScrollCrashPathTests covers both fixed invariants: stable FitsProposedWidth sizing across repeated layout passes, and a disclosure toggle storm interleaved with window resizes settling back to the original collapsed size in a real hosted NSWindow. Ran locally on macOS 27.2 (this verification's runtime); both tests pass.

payload.summary: Verified: inspector closes synchronously before the grid re-renders, eliminating the reflow. Removed the now-dead animated-dismissal handler it superseded and filed KRMA-698 for pre-existing unrelated KeyMonitorTests failures.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Reproduce the layout shift by entering Edit mode and returning to Library without changing the window size or library contents; record which layout elements move or resize.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Implementer reproduced and documented: the mosaic grid resizes because the editor inspector was still presented for one frame when the workspace switched back to grid, then animated closed, causing the grid to lay out beside the inspector before its final width.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Identify the state or measurement change that triggers the unnecessary reflow, such as available space, toolbar/inspector visibility, scroll geometry, or a stale layout measurement.
acceptance_criteria.notes: Root cause: ContentView's onChange(of: viewModel.navigation.mode) closed the inspector with withAnimation only after the mode already flipped to .grid, so SwiftUI rendered the grid at the inspector-constrained width first.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Preserve the Library layout across the transition when its actual inputs have not changed, without suppressing legitimate reflow after window or content changes.
acceptance_criteria.notes: AppViewModel.navigate(to:) now sets inspectorState.isPresented = false before navigation.move(to: .grid), so the grid never renders at the transient inspector-constrained width. Verified via LibraryChromeLayoutTests.testReturningFromEditRestoresTheSameLibraryViewportWidth (viewport width matches pre-edit width mid-transition and after settling).

payload.comment: Root cause: RenderPipeline.applyDetailControls collapsed luminanceNoise and colorNoise with max(), so both controls drove one filter pass and the lower setting was ignored. The mapping also capped CINoiseReduction noiseLevel at 0.1 and attenuated the result again, leaving moderate settings weak. The separate RAW develop path already gates both decoder controls by their is*Supported capabilities, preserves nil decoder defaults, and disables unsupported inspector rows; no RAW path change was needed. Fix: independently map each raster control to its own CINoiseReduction pass (0...0.2 threshold), use each control's Detail/Contrast values, route the single local-mask NR control through one pass, and bump the render cache version. Preview, comparison, and export use this shared pipeline. Reproduction: generated deterministic 96x64 floating-point RGBA input with hard luminance edge plus either luminance-only or chroma-only high-frequency noise; each control at 70. Pixel assertions require at least 20% noise-energy reduction and at least 80% edge contrast retention; zero is pixel-neutral. Results: focused regression passed; RenderPipelineTests 48 passed, 2 skipped; RAWDevelopSettingsTests 4 passed, 2 skipped. Real RAW decoder/apply checks skipped because no local licensed RAW fixture is configured. Commands: swift test --filter RenderPipelineTests/testNoiseReductionReducesLuminanceAndChromaNoiseWithoutLosingTheEdge; swift test --filter RenderPipelineTests; swift test --filter RAWDevelopSettingsTests; git diff --check for changed files. Commit cdbe484.

payload.title: Fix warm 30-cell grid re-entry latency budget miss

payload.comment: Attribution (acceptance criterion 1) from the now-working KRMA-744 harness, commit 8bb287a7. Valid baseline, Release, M1 Pro, macOS 27.0, DSC01019.ARW (126 MB, 9504x6336), 30 warm samples: first pixel p50/p95 652/664 ms vs <= 50 ms; main-actor before first suspension p95 72 ms vs <= 2 ms; confirmed p95 1009 ms. Records: /tmp/kromora-capture/KROMORA-last-known-frame-DSC01019-20261001-101504-report.jsonl. These replace every earlier figure on this ticket. Profile: a 1 ms /usr/bin/sample of the xctest main thread during a 100-sample run puts 37% of ALL main-thread time in AccelerateCrypto_SHA256_compress, every sample of it under ImageSource.makePortableIdentity. For a URL-backed source that calls PortablePhotoSourceFingerprint.file(at:) (PortablePhotoIdentity.swift:65), which does Data(contentsOf:) plus a full SHA-256 of the 126 MB RAW, and SourceImportPlan.source (SourceImportPlan.swift:44) is a computed property, so every access builds a new ImageSource and hashes again. The hash lands at four points of one selection, all on the main actor: inside selectCollectionImage (9.3% of main-thread time; the ~70 ms pre-suspension miss), AppViewModel.load (4.6%), SourceSessionCoordinator.prepare (13.9%), EditedThumbnailCoordinator.request after its yield (9.4%). About half a second of each ~1.4 s handoff cycle is this hash, so most of the 650 ms first pixel, including the exact stored-frame case (627 ms, 0 renders). Suggested direction: makePortableIdentity is passed an existing identity but still recomputes the content hash; reuse it while the file-change signature (size, modification date, resource identifier) is unchanged, and build the plan's ImageSource once. That is an identity-design decision, so keep the KRMA-734 in-place-replacement identity tests green. Not attributed: whatever remains of the first pixel after the hash is gone (Edit-surface mount, inspector construction); re-profile then. Re-run: caffeinate -d, then scripts/run-kromora-capture.sh --benchmark last-known-frame --source realworldtest/DSC01019.ARW --iterations 30, one capture at a time, display unlocked; add KROMORA_LAST_KNOWN_FRAME_ENFORCE_BUDGETS=1 to make a miss fail. Grid miss is split to KRMA-745. Details in docs/TESTING.md.

Harness defects from the verification report are fixed in 8bb287a7 (KRMA-744): grid and Edit samples now remount and wait for real mount/layout, first-pixel/confirmed latencies are re-based to a timestamp before selectCollectionImage with no sleep or polling floor, exact/stale criteria are asserted, default 30 samples, records carry machine/OS/commit/gridMounts/bodyEvaluations, a 30-cell grid is exact, and the window-visibility skip now fires only after a 5 s settle. First valid capture is in docs/TESTING.md (KRMA-744 section): exact PASS, stale PASS, warm grid p95 214 ms (miss, KRMA-745), warm Edit first pixel p95 664 ms and main-actor p95 72 ms (miss, KRMA-743 with root-cause diagnosis). Verifier note: the capture needs an unlocked, awake display (caffeinate -d) and one run at a time. If a run skips with occlusionState=8192, the display is locked/asleep or another window is covering it; this is not a harness defect. Re-verification here is: re-run scripts/run-kromora-capture.sh --benchmark last-known-frame --source realworldtest/DSC01019.ARW --iterations 30, confirm the report.jsonl and LAST_KNOWN_FRAME_BUDGET_SUMMARY exist, then pass the criteria that are about the harness and ticketing (budget misses are tracked in KRMA-743/745 and are not this ticket's pass condition).

Unblocking chain: KRMA-742 (harness) depends on KRMA-744, which is now implemented in 8bb287a7 and handed to review. The required fields and every KRMA-734 budget are now evaluated by one capture (docs/TESTING.md, KRMA-744 section): exact PASS, stale PASS, grid p95 214 ms vs 100 (KRMA-745), warm Edit first pixel p95 664 ms vs 50 and main-actor p95 72 ms vs 2 (KRMA-743). Once KRMA-742 passes verification this ticket's acceptance (release test bundle links, capture records the fields, every budget evaluated, results documented, no target redefined) is met; budget misses are tracked by their own urgent tickets rather than being this ticket's pass condition.

Status after the KRMA-744 harness repair (8bb287a7): the Release benchmark now produces valid, asserted evidence. Budgets: exact warm Edit PASS (0 renders, 1 confirmed), stale warm Edit PASS (1 provisional, 1 confirmed), warm 30-cell grid p95 214 ms vs 100 MISS (KRMA-745), warm Edit first pixel p95 664 ms vs 50 MISS and main-actor before suspension p95 72 ms vs 2 MISS (KRMA-743, root cause identified: whole-file SHA-256 of the 126 MB RAW in ImageSource.makePortableIdentity on the main actor, 37% of main-thread time). Per this ticket both misses are ticketed and linked in depends_on, so it stays open until 743 and 745 land and the capture reports edit=PASS and grid=PASS. Remaining unmeasured budgets from the list (unchanged Look rescan, pixel epoch bump, navigation burst) are not covered by this harness and need their structural CI assertions confirmed at verification. The earlier historical 2026-09-30 grid/Edit latency numbers are invalid and superseded.

Implemented and verified in 8bb287a7. Root cause of the never-completing capture: xctest never finishes launching or drains AppKit's event queue, so the app never activates and the window stays occluded (occlusionState=8192, appActive=false); no number of activate/orderFront calls changes that. Fixed by finishLaunching() + pumping the event queue at every wait (a settle helper) and a 5 s wait for the window to become visible. The intermittent hang (about 1 run in 3, different step each time) was Metal reporting presentedTime==0 for a compositor-skipped drawable, which PreviewSurface deliberately treats as unconfirmed and stops retrying after a bounded number of skips; the harness now sets zeroPresentedTimeFallback like ConcurrentExportEditingBenchmark and reports the count (1-2 per run is normal). payload.comment: Implemented in d556d7c4. SourceSessionCoordinator.begin now starts the stored-edit read at selection and publishes it through a new onStoredDocumentLoaded as soon as it is read (fenced to the active request; a newer selection, cancel, or shutdown drops it); AppViewModel.adoptStoredDocumentValues puts the document, comparison baseline, editor session, and presented crop on the panel under the same pristine-session ownership rule. adoptStoredEdits (source-dependent reconciliation) is unchanged and still runs after preparation; it queues a corrective render only if a render with a different document was already scheduled. A second cause surfaced while reading the code: preparation is serialized behind the previous source, so the edit read used to queue behind it too; starting it in begin fixes that. Acceptance: (1) measured with the new window-independent StoredEditAdoptionBenchmark (real RenderEngine, real DSC01019.ARW, no NSWindow, Release, M1 Pro, 10 samples, ms from selection): panel values p50/p95 295/308 before, 154/197 after; the panel previously received them at exactly the instant preparation finished (lead 0.0 ms) and now leads preparation by about 138 ms, and arrives before first pixel (about 290 ms in the last-known-frame capture). I did not extend the window-based harness, per the measurement note on this ticket. (2) No frame with defaults beside the new photo's edited pixels beyond the first ~150 ms, which is before first pixel; the reset to defaults at selection in beginLoad is unchanged and is KRMA-756's concern. (3) StoredEditAdoptionTests: early adoption while preparation is held, first render uses the stored document (no identity-document render; verified the old code rendered it), and a superseded selection never publishes the old photo's values; all three fail on the previous code. (4) Photo ready p50 915 to 703 ms because the redundant corrective render is gone; exact-hit bypass, histogram admission, and the stale-completion tests are covered by the existing suites, all green. (5) Gate on this tree: warning-gate clean, fast, serial (455), identity (4) all pass; swift format lint and git diff --check clean. Batches process at most eight records; visible editor work takes precedence, normal store activity leaves the sweep eligible, and tests cover cancellation, resumption, multiple ticks, batch limits, and real-frame preservation. Commit da53377. Checks: scripts/ci-tests.sh fast passed; scripts/ci-tests.sh serial ran 464 tests but failed only in RelaunchParityTests.testUnchangedPackageReusesSettledFramesAfterRelaunch (15 assertions tied to KRMA-765). The isolated case fails with scheduler injection disabled as well, confirming it is independent of this change.

payload.summary: Verified; fixed perpetual re-sweep after a completed pass. Serial lane has only pre-existing KRMA-765 RelaunchParity failures.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Sweep scheduled via production idle-work mechanism at lowest priority
acceptance_criteria.notes: ImageWorkScheduler.enqueuePackageIO, .maintenance lane, .background priority

acceptance_criteria.criterion: At most eight files per tick; repeated ticks remove all placeholder frames
Normal store read/write/invalidation does not permanently disable sweep
User-visible work cancels/yields sweep; later idle time resumes
acceptance_criteria.notes: Scheduler priority governs; hasMore state retained across cancellation

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Real frames never removed; concurrent-replacement guards retained
Tests exercise scheduling seam across ticks, cancellation, resumption, bounds, real frames
ci-tests fast and serial pass
acceptance_criteria.notes: Caveat: serial lane is not fully green. Only RelaunchParityTests fails (15 assertions), identically at 0c51841 before this change; tracked by KRMA-765. No new failures. fast passes.

checks_run: scripts/ci-tests.sh serial: only pre-existing RelaunchParityTests failures (15, same count at 0c51841)
findings: medium (fixed): after a sweep pass completed, every later store access re-enqueued a full pass, re-decoding every frame indefinitely; added placeholderSweepCompletedPass in both stores.
fixes: Added placeholderSweepCompletedPass flag in both frame stores so a completed pass is not rescheduled (placeholders cannot be written anymore).

payload.same_agent_warning: Verification agent 'claude' matches the implementation actor; continuing with a warning.

No source changes were made in this pass because those remaining behaviors are outside the store-boundary change and already have dedicated dependent issues; no new commit was created. No display-bound captures were run.

payload.comment:
Implemented and committed as 752a93b5.

The Xcode target now merges App/Info.plist, signs with App/Kromora.entitlements, enables App Sandbox and hardened runtime, and generates the App Store display name, photography category, copyright, and non-exempt-encryption metadata. Release disables Xcode base-entitlement injection so the embedded capability set matches the explicit entitlement file exactly.

Final merged Info.plist keys: BuildMachineOSBuild, CFBundleDevelopmentRegion, CFBundleDisplayName, CFBundleDocumentTypes, CFBundleExecutable, CFBundleIdentifier, CFBundleInfoDictionaryVersion, CFBundleName, CFBundlePackageType, CFBundleShortVersionString, CFBundleSupportedPlatforms, CFBundleVersion, DTCompiler, DTPlatformBuild, DTPlatformName, DTPlatformVersion, DTSDKBuild, DTSDKName, DTXcode, DTXcodeBuild, ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption, LSApplicationCategoryType, LSMinimumSystemVersion, NSHighResolutionCapable, NSHumanReadableCopyright, NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription, NSPrincipalClass, UTExportedTypeDeclarations.

App/Info.plist intentionally retains CFBundleDocumentTypes, CFBundleExecutable, CFBundleIdentifier, CFBundleInfoDictionaryVersion, CFBundleName, CFBundlePackageType, CFBundleShortVersionString, CFBundleVersion, LSMinimumSystemVersion, NSHighResolutionCapable, NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription, NSPrincipalClass, and UTExportedTypeDeclarations. The standard identity/version fields remain because the SwiftPM bundle script copies this plist directly. The script supplies the icon keys itself. Xcode supplies CFBundleDisplayName; the SwiftPM bundle name remains Kromora. KromoraGitCommit is absent from Xcode builds; the About view gracefully shows the version without a commit identifier.

The CryptoKit scan found SHA-256 hashing for identities, checksums, fingerprints, and cache keys; it found no CommonCrypto or SecKey use and no AES-GCM, ChaChaPoly, SymmetricKey, HMAC, seal, or open encryption operations. Content-addressing hashes are not encryption, supporting ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption=false.

Verification passed: unsigned Release build and required merged-plist values; ad-hoc-signed Release with the exact five entitlements, hardened-runtime signature flag, and codesign --verify --deep --strict; scripts/build-macos-app.sh; scripts/verify-library-package-metadata.sh; scripts/ci-tests.sh fast (1,522 tests); git diff --check.

payload.comment: Implemented in c5edcd15: stored-original aspect adoption, diagnostics, and test. Library, thumbnail, relaunch-parity and observability tests pass. The spinner cause is not yet known; relaunch the dev build with the thumbnail-frames log stream described in the ticket and attach the output.

First relaunch capture (thumbnail-frames log): (1) ThumbnailFrameRead lines are cheap (readMs 0-4, applyMs 0-7) and all report original=true, but were visible=false prefetch reads that sat queued ~3000 ms (queueMs 2967-2991); only one visible=true read appears (queueMs 0, applyMs 204). (2) ThumbnailOriginalLoad (provider level) shows dozens of 190-2450 ms loads, completing in a serial staircase (329, 742, 1126, 1509 ms, about 0.4 s apart) with queueMs 1-6 s, i.e. cells waited and then loaded slowly one after another. Cached originals exist for all photos, so these look like source decodes or store-actor waits, but the log could not say which. Follow-up b65954f385684707f03f4643ffc1e87a09dc8d9d adds tier=memory|pack|decode, packOutcome and lookupMs/decodeMs per load. Next capture should answer whether visible cells are decoding source despite valid packed frames.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND from the second capture: every ThumbnailOriginalLoad decode reports packOutcome=rejected.colorSpaceUnpresentable. All 140 stored originals in the reporter's library are tagged displayP3 (the 33 edited frames are sRGB); WorkingSpace.current is sRGB and RasterColorSpace.displayP3.isLosslesslyPresentable(in: .sRGB) is false, so FrameClassifier refused every stored original and each launch re-decoded every unedited photo from source (190-550 ms each, serialised, behind a multi-second queue), then rewrote another P3 frame that would be rejected again. That is why edited photos (sRGB frames) appear instantly and unedited ones spin. Fix in d7f619a3ac3a442df55dcbe63865e589a11cc112: ThumbnailFrameEncoder.normalizedRaster converts to the working space; OriginalThumbnailLoader shows the same normalized pixels. Regression test fails without the fix with the same reason and passes with it; 178 related tests pass. Existing P3 frames self-heal: rejected once, re-decoded, rewritten as sRGB, instant from the second launch. Still open: the 2-3 s queueMs on prefetch frame reads and the 200 ms applyMs on visible reads (suspected aspect-adoption projection invalidation); recheck after one warm relaunch.

Verification capture after d7f619a3 (relaunch with frames already rewritten): zero ThumbnailOriginalLoad lines, so no source decodes at all; every cell is served from packed frames. Visible-photo ThumbnailFrameRead now queueMs 0-8, readMs 0-1, applyMs 0-3 (was applyMs about 200). Remaining: the first batch of 12 prefetch reads (visible=false, issued about 5 s before the visible reads at 12:32:01) waits queueMs 2340-3334 and shows applyMs 98-196, rising per batch. Candidate causes: scheduler lane starvation by launch work, and one projection invalidation per adopted aspect on the main actor. Not blocking; reporter says launch is much better.

Follow-up f9add390ae9df09318f3c58f931554cb1b64b127 logs the individual steps inside the two 50 ms blocks.

ROOT CAUSE FOUND via the KRMA-869 photo-switch timeline: loadSyncPrefix planMs was 49-50 ms in every switch and selectPortableItem collectionSelectMs came in multiples of ~50 ms (0/50/98/252). ImageSource.makePortableIdentity compared the persisted PhotoSourceFingerprint with a fresh one using ==; the package JSON coder stores dates as ISO-8601 whole seconds (asset.json: 2026-10-09T16:17:37Z, file mtime 16:17:37.384), so they never matched, and every open (and every adjacent-photo ImageSource) fell through to PortablePortableSourceFingerprint.file, a whole-file SHA-256 on the main actor (~50 ms for a 126 MB ARW). Stat plus the 64 KiB sample digest was measured at under 1 ms, so it was not the cause. Fix 2eaef446ef1bd68bede1bfba7bc952831923acfd switches to isSameFileSnapshot (existing, tolerates sub-second truncation); test fails without it. Expect the synchronous span to fall from about 100 ms to a few ms; re-measure with lkf-direct and the photo-switch log.

A post-fix capture (14:13) still showed planMs=49 and collectionSelectMs=254. All 105 library assets whose files are present compare equal with isSameFileSnapshot (probe against the reporter's library), so the likely cause is a stale binary. 871d216d7028a7933d95d889b1555760361ce968 adds a PhotoSwitchPhase wholeFileRehash line (hashMs, hadStoredSignature, mainThread) on the expensive path: if it never appears during a Library to Edit switch the rehash is gone; if it does, that line says why.

The wholeFileRehash log (14:30 capture) showed the first fix was not the whole story: dozens of 49-52 ms whole-file hashes on the MAIN THREAD, hadStoredSignature=true, about 35 back to back at idle with no switch, plus 3-7 inside every photo switch (collectionSelectMs 246-254, planMs 48-50). Cause: browsing assets carry a real content hash but a placeholder change signature (PhotoAsset init(browsingPortableAsset:), no byteCount/mtime/resourceIdentifier), so no comparison can succeed. Callers: EditedThumbnailCoordinator (x2), PreviewAdmissionCoordinator adjacent prefetch, IdleFrameWarmer candidates, AppViewModel.openImage. 0b152709dc116a1db407b6fd411d04f08e6a8528 keeps the stored hash for that case; legacy browsing-v1 identities still hash. Off-main rehashes (hadStoredSignature=false, mainThread=false) in source preparation remain and could reuse the record's persisted sourceChangeSignature as a follow-up. 501 related tests pass.

Post-fix capture (15:13, dev build, three Library to Edit switches). selectPortableItem 2.4 ms (was 50.8), selectionSyncReturned 2.8 ms (was 100.9, 303.8 in one run), planMs 0 (was 49-50), collectionSelectMs 1-2 (was 0/50/98/252), beginLoadScheduled 32 ms (was 520, so the old 420 ms gap was main-thread starvation by the rehashes, not SwiftUI), sourcePrepared 131-180 ms (was 500-580), firstPixel storedFrame 74/192/205 ms (was 1,313-1,955), rendered confirm 609-640 ms. No wholeFileRehash on the main thread; the remaining ones are off-main in source preparation (hadStoredSignature=false, 50-62 ms each).

Result of the KRMA-860 fixes as seen in the photo-switch timeline: first pixel for a Library to Edit switch went from about 1.3-1.95 s to 74-205 ms and the synchronous main-actor span from about 100 ms to under 3 ms. Remaining items: the off-main whole-file rehash in source preparation (about 50-60 ms of the 131-180 ms sourcePrepared) and the rendered confirmation at about 610-640 ms.

payload.comment: Handoff to verification (implementer: claude; reporter has reviewed). Commits 2eaef446, 871d216d, 0b152709. The 99 ms main-actor stall before the first suspension was whole-file SHA-256 hashing on the main thread: ImageSource compared a persisted file-change signature with == (package dates are whole seconds, so it never matched), and browsing assets carry a placeholder signature, so every ImageSource built by edited-thumbnail requests, adjacent-preview prefetch, the idle warmer and open rehashed the file (about 50 ms for a 126 MB ARW; about 35 in a row at idle). Fixes: use the existing tolerant isSameFileSnapshot; keep the stored content hash when the signature is a browsing observation and the identity is real (legacy browsing-v1 identities still hash); log wholeFileRehash. Evidence from the KRMA-869 timeline on the reporter's library: selection sync 100.9 ms -> 2.8 ms, planMs 49 -> 0, beginLoadScheduled 520 -> 32 ms, first pixel 1.3-1.95 s -> 74-205 ms. Tests: ImageSourceIdentityReuseTests (4; the round-trip test fails without the fix), plus 501 related identity/thumbnail/preview/relaunch tests green. Check: the new tests, the reasoning on trusting the stored hash for package-embedded originals, and that the off-main rehash in source preparation (hadStoredSignature=false) is acceptable or worth a follow-up.

Handoff to verification (implementer: claude; reporter has reviewed). Commits c5edcd15, b65954f3, d7f619a3. Root cause of unedited photos spinning on launch: ImageIO returns library thumbnails in Display P3, the working space is sRGB, and a P3 raster is never lossless there, so FrameClassifier rejected all 140 stored originals (colorSpaceUnpresentable) and every launch re-decoded every unedited photo from source. Fix: ThumbnailFrameEncoder.normalizedRaster converts to the working space and OriginalThumbnailLoader shows the same pixels. Also: an unresolved cell takes its aspect ratio from the stored original frame (Item.adoptStoredOriginalAspect), removing the 4:3 placeholder reflow, and ThumbnailFrameRead/ThumbnailOriginalLoad diagnostics (category thumbnail-frames) with tier=memory|pack|decode and packOutcome. Verified on the reporter's library: after one rewrite launch no ThumbnailOriginalLoad decodes, visible reads queueMs 0-8, applyMs 0-3. Tests: LibraryGridTests aspect adoption, ThumbnailTests P3 regression (fails without the fix with the same reason), 178 related tests green. Check: existing P3 frames self-heal on first launch; sRGB conversion may clip very saturated colors slightly; prefetch reads still queued 2-4 s at launch (noted, not blocking).

Handoff to verification (implementer: claude; reporter has reviewed). Commit ea9b6f47. CropToolbarControls placed three unioned glass buttons (Save, Cancel, Undo) in a GlassEffectContainer with no stack, so they could lay out vertically and draw one tall orange capsule hiding Save and Cancel after the Xcode 27 beta / macOS 27.2 update. Fix: an explicit HStack(spacing: 10) around them; behavior, help text, accessibility and union id unchanged. The reporter's later screenshot shows the group as a proper row. Tests: MenuCommandTests, CropInspectorTests pass. Check: the toolbar group is vertically centred and a single glass group in light and dark.

Handoff to verification (implementer: claude; reporter has reviewed). Commit a9607f31. The Landscape orientation button had no icon because rectangle.landscape is not an SF Symbol (rectangle.portrait exists; landscape is plain rectangle), verified with NSImage(systemSymbolName:) on macOS 27.2. Fix: static landscapeOrientationSymbol = rectangle and portraitOrientationSymbol on CropInspectorView, plus CropInspectorTests.testOrientationButtonsUseSymbolsThatExist. I also scanned every string literal in Sources that looks like an SF Symbol name; this was the only missing one (dynamically built names such as tab.iconName were not enumerated). Check: both buttons show icons.

Handoff to verification (implementer: claude; reporter has reviewed and chose 'toolbar only'). Commit 17f2ada8. Removed the duplicate Cancel/Save bar and the onDone parameter from CropInspectorView (InfoInspectorView call site updated); Save/Cancel/Undo live only in the window toolbar. Return and Escape still apply/cancel through the global key monitor in KeyboardShortcuts.swift. Handoff to verification (implementer: claude; reporter has reviewed). Commit 9816b8d8. Culling keys (P/X/U/0-5) and the Library culling bar now apply to every selected photo, in the Edit filmstrip and the Library grid, and no longer auto-advance. ImageCollection: cullingTargetIDs, setFlagForSelection, setRatingForSelection (only changed photos recorded, selection and active photo kept); undo stack holds one group per action so one undo reverts a batch; lastCullingAssetIDs drives catalog persistence in LibraryBrowsingCoordinator, which now persists every changed photo (previously only the last) and reports 'N photos: ...'. AppViewModel.perform(_:) is the single entry point for culling keys. The advance: parameter remains for explicit callers and existing tests. Handoff to verification (implementer: claude; reporter has reviewed). Commit c7de04e0. The main window now remembers its size and position: Presentation/WindowFrameAutosave.swift is an NSViewRepresentable anchor that calls setFrameUsingName then setFrameAutosaveName("KromoraMainWindow") on the hosting NSWindow, applied as a background of the root view; defaultSize 1200x800 still seeds the first launch. payload.title: Smart Mask Discovery: develop a signature visual experience beyond the initial prototype

payload.comment:
Initial prototype implemented in the originating chat on 2026-10-12. This is a starting point, not a completed or visually accepted feature. The user has described it as "a start but pretty underwhelming," and requested that the work be captured in the backlog.

What is already implemented:

- `Models/MaskDiscoveryState.swift`: a separate observable presentation boundary with request IDs and waiting, resolved-reference, and ending states. Stale completions and teardown cannot overwrite a newer request. Timing envelopes handle immediate results and indefinite waits without reporting analysis progress.
- `ViewModels/MaskingWorkflowCoordinator.swift`: narrow presentation hooks for both `createSmartMask` and `addSmartMaskComponent`, plus reset on cancellation/source switch, supersession, shutdown, and the existing Info-inspector handoff. Successful mask recipes still commit immediately; the animation does not gate that commit.
- `Views/MaskDiscoveryOverlay.swift`: a separate transparent `MTKView` over the existing canvas. It consumes the state and an injected asynchronous stored-pixel reader, rather than depending on the mask-generation engine. The GPU device is shared with presentation, but the animation owns its pipeline, command queue, textures, timers, and explicit teardown.
- `Resources/MaskDiscovery.metal`: faint, slowly drifting interference ribbons while waiting; a color wash and moving boundary glint reveal the returned coverage, then recede. Current reveal duration is 1.65 seconds. These visual choices are provisional and should be revisited.
- `Models/MaskDiscoveryGeometry.swift`: an inverse projective mapping for rotation, flips, straighten, perspective, crop, pan/zoom, and backing scale; a disposable 8-bit display mask capped at 512 pixels on the longest edge. Original analysis pixels retain their existing precision and ownership.
- Rendering is bounded to a 960-pixel drawable longest edge, 24 fps normally / 12 under power or thermal constraints, and one frame in flight. Waiting frames use the transparent shader only and do not rerender the photograph. Hidden/inactive windows pause animation. Reduce Motion uses a still treatment. Power/thermal notifications explicitly hop to the main actor; observers/timers are removed during teardown.
- `Views/PreviewView.swift`: mounts the overlay in the edited masking canvas, excludes original comparison/crop/loading presentations, and injects the existing stored-pixel reader. Discovery is discarded on presentation teardown.
- `scripts/build-metal-libraries.sh`, `KromoraPresentation.metallib`, and its checksum: include and precompile the new shader. No runtime shader-source compilation was added.
- `docs/ENGINEERING_GUIDE.md`: documents discovery ownership, resource limits, and separation from analysis/edit/export state.

The underlying files in `Models/PhotoAnalysis` and the existing `Views/PreviewSurface.swift` renderer were not changed for this prototype. Existing analysis, provider, segmentation, caching, and render implementation were preserved. Unrelated retouch, preview-admission, and DispatchGraph changes were left untouched.

Verification already completed:

- Final strict application build: `swift build --scratch-path /tmp/kromora-discovery-build -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors` — passed, zero application compiler warnings.
- Final selected test run: `swift test --scratch-path /tmp/kromora-discovery-build --no-parallel --filter 'MaskDiscoveryTests|MaskingWorkflowCoordinatorTests|MetalKernelParityTests|GeometryPointMappingTests|CanvasNavigationTests|PackageSettingsTests|XcodeProjectInvariantTests'` — 70 tests passed, zero failures.
- Coverage includes request supersession/cancellation, empty/failure exits, immediate commit and component insertion, short/long timing envelopes, geometry mapping, raster orientation/memory cap, resource freshness and shader loading, plus real offscreen GPU checks proving asymmetric actual coverage, transparent photo perimeter, bounded waiting opacity, and complete reveal fade-out.
- `scripts/build-metal-libraries.sh --check` and `git diff --check` — passed.
- Final `scripts/app-store-build.sh` — passed; packaged app resources, arm64 executable, signature, and entitlements verified. Build emits the existing AppIntents metadata-extraction notice because there is no AppIntents dependency.
- Offscreen waiting frames were inspected over the repository's golden-hour landscape fixture. This only establishes a basic static visual check; it does not establish exceptional motion/choreography or user acceptance.
- `swift build --build-tests -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors` encountered an unrelated pre-existing unused `name` variable in `Tests/KromoraKitTests/ColorMixerTests.swift:193`. That file was not modified. The normal selected tests and strict application-only build passed.

Open work and limitations:

- The user has not accepted the visual result; their underwhelming assessment is the principal remaining issue. Treat the current effect as replaceable scaffolding and develop the visual direction further.
- There has been no supervised live GPU-contention benchmark during Apple's analysis, no quantified near-zero-interference result, and no completed live visual review across diverse photographs/canvas sizes.
- The prototype is still uncommitted in the shared working tree. No branch, commit, push, PR, or distribution was created for this work. This backlog ticket records it without claiming implementation completion or moving it to review.

payload.title: Replace global NSEvent key monitor with Commands + focus-scoped key handling (fix system alert beep on hotkeys)
Spike: determine beep-free key handling mechanism (menu key equivalents vs onKeyPress vs key NSView)

payload.comment:
Findings (real NSWindow + NSApp.sendEvent; beep path observed via NSWindow.noResponder(for: keyDown:), the AppKit hook that beeps by default). Test: KeyRoutingProbeTests (serial lane).
1. Bug reproduced: plain 'c' and arrows reach the beep path when NSButton / NSSegmentedControl / NSSlider is first responder and nothing claims them.
2. Plain-letter menu key equivalent = AppKit's last chance before the beep: fires from NSButton/NSSegmentedControl/NSSlider with no beep, does NOT fire while a text field is editing (c and Shift+A both typed normally), and a DISABLED item still swallows the key (no beep). This contradicts the stale comment in MenuCommands.swift (L17-20). NSPopUpButton type-select swallows letters itself (no beep).
3. Arrow menu key equivalents fire from every control including an editing NSTextField, so arrows cannot be menu-only (would steal caret movement).
4. SwiftUI .onKeyPress(phases: .all) on a focused surface: .handled = no beep, key-down and key-up both delivered; .ignored = beep. Only reaches keys while SwiftUI focus is on/under that surface; an NSControl first responder elsewhere still beeps (see 1).
5. A custom key NSView as first responder claims plain keys and arrows (no beep, no menu needed), but is not required for the bulk of the work.
Recommendation for KRMA-920:
- Layer A: plain letters/digits/brackets (c, v, i, q, g, e, b, l, r, p, x, u, 0-5, [ ]) and shifted/modified commands become Commands menu items with .keyboardShortcut (unmodified/shift). Delete/Return/Esc remain in Layer B.
- Layer B: focusable editor surface with .onKeyPress(phases: .all), always returning .handled for owned keys (arrows, Space hold, Esc ladder, Return, Delete, ⌘\ hold). Pure-click toolbar controls (workspace picker, culling menu) must refuse first responder (.focusable(false)) so arrows are not stranded on an NSControl; keep value-editing controls (slider/stepper/text) focusable.
- Residual risk: arrows with a toolbar NSControl focused in the real app (SwiftUI focus vs AppKit first responder). KRMA-920 must verify with the real-app focus path and, if needed, gate arrow menu equivalents on a text-input-active focused value as fallback.

payload.comment: Audit: withWriterMutationLock callers: PortablePackageEditSidecar (replaceSourceFingerprint, commitEditRevision, repairPresentedAspectRatioShard, repairCaptureMetadataShard, selectEditRevision) and PortableLibrarySession (writeVirtualCopy, removeFromLibrary/writeRemoval, writeLibraryState). Contending threads in production (scheduler always present): package-I/O worker, EditDocumentStore actor, detached maintenance/backfill tasks. Worst-case hold: seconds (virtual copy hashes a 100+ MB original); typical tens of ms (F_FULLFSYNC). Main actor: after KRMA-931..934 production mutations route through the scheduler or detached tasks; the main actor only reaches the lock via scheduler-less inline fallbacks (tests) and the sync updateLibraryState/removeFromLibrary/replaceSourceFingerprint APIs, which have no production callers. So contention is possible among background threads, not main. Fix: replaced the OSAllocatedUnfairLock with a serial DispatchQueue(qos: .utility).sync (blocks in kernel, no spin, QoS donation); invariant documented on the method. Test: testConcurrentWriterMutationsOnOneLeaseSerializeWithoutCorruptingShard (peak concurrency 1, no lost read-modify-write updates, package reopens). ci-tests.sh fast exit 0; swift build clean. Note: review M5 'burns CPU' is imprecise (os_unfair_lock waiters sleep), but long holds are still against its intended use.

payload.comment:
Verification review (codex): I audited all call sites. PortablePackageEditSidecar locks replaceSourceFingerprint, commitEditRevision, repairPresentedAspectRatioShard, repairCaptureMetadataShard, and selectEditRevision. PortableLibrarySession locks the markVirtualCopy transaction in writeVirtualCopy, removal through removeFromLibrary/writeRemoval, and writeLibraryState.

The longest protected work is repairCaptureMetadataShard: it reads metadata from each embedded original in the shard that needs repair, then commits one shard. This can take seconds on a large or slow library; ordinary journaled writes include F_FULLFSYNC and typically take tens of milliseconds. Virtual-copy import and original hashing happen before entering the gate, so they do not add to its hold time; I corrected the method documentation in verification commit f9f19cee.

Production contenders are the package-I/O scheduler worker, EditDocumentStore actor, and detached maintenance/backfill tasks. The serial per-lease queue prevents overlapping read-modify-write transactions and waits without spinning. After KRMA-931 through KRMA-934, production does not call the synchronous main-actor mutation APIs or scheduler-less inline fallbacks, so the main actor does not wait on this queue in production. Tests or scheduler-less sessions can exercise those synchronous paths while another mutation is active.

payload.comment: No pool shipped; the per-render allocation in RenderEngineResources.makeProcessingTexture stays. The ticket requires proving a fence before any pool lands, and I can't. Completed textures leave the engine (RenderEngine.swift:560, :2133) and PreviewSurface retains them in at least six places: presentationTexture, transitionTexture, lastValidPresentationTexture, retainedCompleteTexture, pendingPresentationMaterialization, and the histogram readback path. Nothing in the engine is told when those owners release a texture or when GPU completion happens, so a pool could hand out storage that is still being read, which corrupts pixels. No profile shows allocation cost either. A pool would first need an explicit lease/release protocol from the presentation owners. That is a separate design task. No code changed and no tests or benchmarks were run.

payload.comment:
Decision: Keep full-copy virtual copies for MVP. Each copy has its own package asset and independent edits/history, but it also reimports and hashes the full original; a 100 MB RAW therefore adds roughly 100 MB per copy. The project owner accepts this storage cost to keep per-asset ownership and package operations simple.

Sharing would require a package-format change so multiple assets can reference a single original, plus migration of existing copies. Delete, trash, reclaim, and quarantine must retain the source until the last dependent copy is removed. Backup, restore, and integrity validation must preserve and verify shared references without dangling or missing originals.

No shared-original design is planned for MVP. Revisit if concrete user demand shows the storage cost is a problem.

sRGB path trace (code reading):
- Preview: RenderEngine builds the graph with space = WorkingSpace.current (.sRGB); LUT interpolation uses that space (CubeLUT.makeFilter -> inputColorSpace). PreviewSurface.makePresentationTexture renders the CIImage into a bgra8Unorm texture with colorSpace sRGB, so texture bytes are sRGB-encoded. The MTKView is bgra8Unorm with view.colorspace = sRGB (KRMA-923, PreviewSurface.swift ~1180), so Core Animation/WindowServer converts sRGB -> connected-display profile. The CI fallback draw path also renders with frame.space (sRGB).
- Export: RenderEngine.encode uses outputSpace = exportOptions.colorSpace ?? request.space (sRGB by default; ExportWorkflowCoordinator uses .current). createCGImage(..., colorSpace: sRGB) -> CGImageDestination, so the file carries sRGB pixels and an sRGB profile.
- Same graph, same LUT interpolation space, same sRGB encoding on both sides. The only difference is the display transform, done by the system for the preview and by the viewer for the file. Conclusion: the default sRGB preview and export agree in design; no concrete gap found.

Limits of verification: the display transform happens in the compositor and cannot be asserted deterministically in unit tests (needs a real display/colorimeter). Existing tests (WorkingSpaceTests, ColorPipelineTests) cover the enum plumbing and LUT-space propagation only, which is not evidence of end-to-end display accuracy. Residual risk is covered by the release-time display evidence in docs/TESTING.md, not a new ticket.

Display P3 export: the model (ExportFormat capabilities, ExportOptions) accepts .displayP3 for JPEG/HEIF/PNG/TIFF, but no UI exposes it and nothing in the app sets it (options are built with .current). If enabled, the preview would NOT represent it: the canvas is always sRGB, and export would also interpolate LUTs in P3 (buildImage gets outputSpace) so Look results differ from the preview, and derived LUTs are fitted in sRGB. Recommendation: defer Display P3 export (keep it unexposed, ideally reject it at the model level only when a UI is proposed) until the editor can preview P3 accurately; that belongs to a future P3 working-space plan, which is out of scope here. HDR/EDR excluded.

payload.comment: Implemented in 07dbfc1a. Root cause (deterministic, generated fixture; not the user's photo): RenderEngineResources.canonicalPreviewRaster, which builds the stored post-crop first frame, scaled by one uniform factor and rasterized a rounded-size rect. When extent*scale rounded up, the last column/row was only partially covered (alpha 154 on the right edge for 149x202 at longEdge 97); JPEG encoding dropped the alpha, so the stored frame painted a light line on open until the settled render replaced it. Probed and ruled out: makeCIImage preview and makeThumbnailCGImage rasters for fractional, 16:9 and rotated crops at four target sizes (all four edges fully opaque), and the Metal quad/sampler (clampToEdge). Fix: scale each axis to the exact rounded pixel size; crop geometry and frame dimensions unchanged, so KRMA-838's crop-aware policy and KRMA-754's thumbnail fringe are untouched. Regression: CanonicalPreviewRasterEdgeCoverageTests. Tests: RenderEngine/LatestPreviewFrameStore/FirstFrame/PreviewSurface/edge-coverage/Derive suites, 124 run, 0 failures, 3 opt-in skipped. Not done: no live app visual check and no display capture (per CLAUDE.md); the frame is whichever step of the stored-frame first paint the user sees, so a live confirm on a previously saved cropped photo is still worthwhile. Note KRMA-754's thumbnail fringe fill still handles only top/bottom rows; probes showed no partial left/right columns, so left unchanged.

payload.comment: Findings (local fixtures in realworldtest/): Apple Silicon host DNG x5 + HEIC and mirrorless camera ARW x2 all report Display P3 via ImageIO/Core Image. For RAW that is the CIRAWFilter develop space, not an embedded ICC profile; the HEIC is 8-bit with a real Display P3 profile and takes the standard (non-RAW) path. Pipeline: source is converted to WorkingSpace.current (sRGB); wide-gamut values survive as extended floats until the final sRGB encode and the [0,1] CIColorCube domain. Measured (800px, P3 render vs sRGB-encoded round trip, scratch scripts, not committed): 1.2-13% of pixels differ >2/255 and 0.02-3.3% differ >8/255; max ~50/255 (saturated HEIC). Out-of-sRGB pixels: ARW 0%, DNG 0-4.4%, HEIC 1.5%. Recommendation: retain the color-managed sRGB canvas for the Instagram-first MVP; a P3 migration must move WorkingSpace.current, derive LUT fitting (RecipeExtractor), LUT interpolation, frame signatures/caches, thumbnails and export tagging together with parity tests. Not done: no colorimeter/hardware validation; no regression test added because no code changed and no regression was confirmed; no follow-up ticket created, since the decision is to defer. Decision recorded in docs/ENGINEERING_GUIDE.md (9720b06a).

payload.comment: Follow-up in 70d282b5 for the sample.arw first-frame movement. Cause (static trace plus unit test; not reproduced on the user's photo): since bb01e0c3 the stored frame keeps whole pixels only (floor), so its pixel aspect differs from the cropped photo's true aspect by up to one stored pixel. AppViewModel presented it with an extent equal to its own pixel size, while the settled render uses the planned extent, so the canvas fit rect moved by up to about 1 px when the render replaced it. Fix: AppViewModel.storedFramePresentationExtent declares the persisted PresentedGeometry.orientedAspectRatio on the raster's long axis (only when it disagrees by <=1 px). Crop geometry, raster pixels, KRMA-754 thumbnail fringe and KRMA-838 candidate policy are unchanged; no stored-format change. Regression: StoredFrameExtentTests (landscape, portrait, >1px disagreement keeps raster size). Ran StoredFrameExtent, PreviewSurface, FirstFramePresentation, WarmReopenPresentation, PresentationBudget, CanonicalPreviewRaster suites: 92 tests, 0 failures. Not verified: no live check on sample.arw and I did not launch the app against the user's library. One assumption remains: the persisted aspect comes from the preview-render extent, so if it differs from the planned crop aspect by more than the stored-pixel rounding, a residual shift could remain. Human visual confirmation on sample.arw is still required.

Root cause isolated (2026-10-22). Debug capture (scratch copy only, repo untouched) at the app's export call (ExportCoordinator.performBatchExport; the single-photo File > Export goes through the batch path, not performExport). Captured: item.document present (live snapshot) with isPerAsset=true; the in-session EditDocument is IDENTICAL to the persisted revision-1 document (0 JSON diffs; one Heal spot, seed 1063, point 0.58/0.13, radius 0.00446, feather 0.35, opacity 1). Source the app hands the engine: ImageSource.resolve(url:, nativeExtent: .zero) (ExportCoordinator.sourceAccess, by design), assetID portable:1e7aa3f2-..., identity decoderVersion imageio-standard-v1. The KRMA-1085/1076 harness and probes instead used nativeExtent = 8064x6048. Heal output depends on source.nativeExtent; RenderPipeline passes source.nativeExtent as retouchSourceSize/sourceSize downstream (RenderPipeline.swift ~143/180/196) while the comment in ExportCoordinator.sourceAccess says the pipeline never reads that field, so the nativeExtent-zero contract is violated. Fix (Sources/KromoraKit/Models/RenderEngine.swift): new sourceWithDecodedExtent(_:) resolves the decoder's extent via ImageSource.withNativeExtent when the declared extent is unusable, applied at the top of pickRetouchSource and retouchAnalysisProxy. RenderPipeline.render no longer forwards a zero nativeExtent as retouchSourceSize/sourceSize (nil when undeclared). Tests (RetouchExportBoundaryTests): testAutomaticHealSourceDoesNotDependOnDeclaredNativeExtent and testExportPixelsDoNotDependOnDeclaredNativeExtent; both fail on the original code (export differs by 2514 pixels, max 15) and pass with the fix.
